thread:
Alyssa: Pushed a short RFC addendum for a "transport compatibility bridge" to unify streaming safetensors and legacy tar/gz checkpoints. Main idea: adapter that normalizes byte-range reads, chunk manifests, and exposes an optional zero-copy path. Sketch + diagram: https://go/internal/rfc/transport-bridge

Sam K: Skimmed it. Biggest concern is double-copy for gzipped checkpoints when we materialize chunks to match safetensors layout. That hits both latency and memory. :thinking:

Jia: What if we prefer sidecar indexes for tar variants and canonicalize byte ranges at CDN/origin? Pros: no runtime decompression in the loader. Cons: requires pre-ingest work and extra metadata per checkpoint.

Marta: From the early bench I ran, the adapter adds ~8-12% wall-time on first warmup for a 4GB model when we stream+decompress on the fly, but it saved ~15% storage since we avoided full materialization. Numbers vary by network.

Alyssa: Agreed. The tradeoff doc says: prefer zero-copy mmap path for native safetensors; for tar.gz fallback we try streaming decompressor that feeds KV cache directly without writing to disk. Only fall back to temp buffers when memory pressure prevents streaming.

Sam K: I think we should expose a tiny transport API so loaders can optimize without knowing formats. Pseudo: 
```
Transport::read_chunk(manifest_id, chunk_id) -> Future<ReadBuf>
if transport.supports_range() { use HTTP Range } else { fetch whole file + slice }
```
Also add supports_lazy_decompress flag so caller can choose streaming vs buffer.

Jia: Good call. Also keep manifest parsing out of hot path; transports should return pre-parsed chunk descriptors for the loader to avoid repeated parsing. That keeps interface boundaries clean.

Marta: Ops question — can this be per-deployment? Private customers might prefer disk-backed temp files for auditing/compliance instead of in-memory streams.

Alyssa: Yup, per-tenant config + feature flag. Next steps I proposed: (1) microbench PR that implements supports_lazy_decompress on s3/http transports, (2) add Transport::prefetch_hint(manifest_id, chunk_range), (3) integration test exercising eviction while streaming.

deploy-bot: created ticket INF-482: "transport-compat microbench + flag" and assigned to @Alyssa. :white_check_mark:

Sam K: I'll prototype a small streaming decompressor shim today and drop notes in the PR.

Alyssa: Thanks — want to keep this lightweight. If we can get the microbench results within a week we can decide whether the adapter lives in runtime or as a sidecar preprocessor.

Jia: Adding a doc comment: avoid format-specific header parsing in Transport. Let the manifest service surface a normalized chunk manifest.

Marta: +1. Ops will test with a private cluster once the flag exists.

Alyssa: Awesome. If no blockers I'll open the PR tomorrow.
